initial_inventory.title: sm70: instantiate the E4M3 GEMM at quantization groups 64 and 32

metadata.title: sm70: instantiate the E4M3 GEMM at quantization groups 64 and 32
metadata.body:
## What

Let the SM70 block-FP8 GEMM run at quantization groups 64 and 32.

The TurboMind operand templates already take `GroupSizeU`/`GroupSizeV`
(`arch/config_sm70_s884.h`, `CHUNK_K = lcm(lcm(Gu, Gv), CTA_K)`), and the 4-bit
registry instantiates groups 64 and 32. The E4M3 registry listed group 128
only, and both fp8 entry points refused anything else, so a block-FP8 weight
whose N or K is not a multiple of 128 could not run at all - not slower, not at
all.

- `kernel/sm70_884_8.cu`: the 13 `Config_E4M3` entries duplicated at groups 64
  and 32.
- `ops/awq_sm70_gemm.cu`: `fp8_sm70_prepare` and `fp8_gemm_sm70_out` accept
  32, 64 or 128. Callers that pass 128 take exactly the same path as before.

## Why

On a V100 deployment driven through SGLang, several dense projections are
FP16 because their shapes miss the 128 block. Four of them, at M=4 (decode),
against the fp16 linear each replaces:

| shape | block | fp16 | fp8 | rel err |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2560x160 | 32 | 14.6 us | 6.7 us | 2.61e-2 |
| 1152x288 | 32 | 15.4 us | 7.8 us | 2.62e-2 |
| 864x1152 | 32 | 17.7 us | 11.4 us | 2.66e-2 |
| 320x2560 | 64 | 18.9 us | 15.9 us | 2.66e-2 |

Accuracy is flat against the group-128 control on the same data (2.74e-2), so
the finer block costs nothing numerically here. At the call counts one
Flash-Next decode step makes, that is about **1.0 ms of a 25.9 ms step**.

## Notes

- The kernel patch was developed and measured against the SM70 subset this
  repository publishes; the two changed translation units compile clean with the
  same flags (`-arch=sm_70`, CUTLASS headers as configured by
  `scripts/build_sm70_turbomind.py`).
- The caller side (choosing a block per layer, probing support at load) lives in
  the downstream layer, not here; a build without these entries keeps refusing
  sub-128 groups with the same error as today.
